_meta.indication: KIMMTRAK is indicated for the treatment of HLA-A*02:01-positive adult patients with unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized (2:1), controlled, multi-center trial of tebentafusp versus investigator's choice (dacarbazine, ipilimumab, or pembrolizumab), stratified by LDH status.
pivotal_trials.population: HLA-A*02:01-positive adults with advanced (metastatic) uveal melanoma, previously untreated in the metastatic setting (1L).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: overall survival (OS); secondary: PFS, BOR, DCR by RECIST v1.1.
pivotal_trials.result: OS favored tebentafusp: median 21.7 vs 16.0 months; HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.37, 0.71); p<0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥ 30%) were cytokine release syndrome, rash, pyrexia, pruritus, fatigue, nausea, chills, abdominal pain, edema, hypotension, dry skin, headache, and vomiting. CRS occurred in 89% of KIMMTRAK patients (0.8% Grade 3/4) and rash in 83% (18% Grade 3/4). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 28% of patients; one patient (0.4%) had a fatal reaction (pulmonary embolism).
target_moa: Tebentafusp is a bispecific gp100 peptide-HLA-directed CD3 T cell engager; its TCR arm binds a gp100 peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 on uveal melanoma cells and its anti-CD3 arm redirects polyclonal T cells to lyse the gp100-expressing tumor cells.
modality: Bispecific fusion protein (soluble TCR fused to an anti-CD3 scFv).

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), which may be serious or life-threatening; monitor for at least 16 hours following the first three infusions.

companion_dx_detail: Patients are selected based on a positive HLA-A*02:01 genotyping test; the SeCore® HLA Sequencing System and uTYPE® Dx v1.0 HLA Sequence Analysis Software (Thermo Fisher Scientific) were used to identify HLA-A*02:01-positive patients, though an FDA-approved test was not available at approval.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the review team did not refer the application to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee.

It was a traditional (non-accelerated) approval based on a statistically significant OS improvement in the pivotal Phase 3 Study 202.
